title: CASE Statements

comicStory.title: The Teacher's Grading Problem

panels.text: Imagine you're a teacher grading students 📊
Marks: 90 → Grade A, 75 → Grade B, 50 → Grade C, 30 → Fail
Problem: Numbers alone are hard to understand
Solution: Convert marks into meaningful categories
This is CASE STATEMENT! Apply conditions like IF-ELSE in SQL
Aha Moment: CASE = 'If this → then that' logic 🔥

comicStory.twist: Raw numbers mean nothing without context. CASE transforms data into insights!
comicStory.lesson: CASE statements apply IF-ELSE logic to transform and categorize data dynamically.

deepDive.whatItIs: CASE is a conditional expression in SQL used to apply logic like IF-ELSE. It allows you to transform data based on conditions within your queries.
deepDive.whyItMatters: In real companies, raw data needs interpretation. Business rules must be applied, and reporting needs readable output. CASE statements bridge the gap between raw data and business insights.
whereUsed: Data transformation - Convert codes to readable labels
Business rules - Apply grading, categorization, segmentation
Data cleaning - Handle NULL values, standardize formats
ETL pipelines - Transform data during loading

visualExamples.title: Simple CASE - Direct Value Matching
visualExamples.description: Compare one column against specific values
visualExamples.diagram:
CASE status
  WHEN 'A' THEN 'Active'
  WHEN 'I' THEN 'Inactive'
  ELSE 'Unknown'
END

visualExamples.title: Searched CASE - Conditional Logic (MOST USED)
visualExamples.diagram:
CASE
  WHEN salary > 100000 THEN 'High'
  WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN 'Medium'
  ELSE 'Low'
END

visualExamples.title: CASE with Aggregation
visualExamples.diagram: SUM(CASE WHEN status='paid' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) as total_paid

visualExamples.title: Salary Categorization Example
visualExamples.description: Convert salary into categories: >100k → High, 50k-100k → Medium, <50k → Low

keyPoints: CASE works like IF-ELSE in programming
Searched CASE is most flexible (allows any condition)
Simple CASE compares one column to values
Always include ELSE to avoid NULL results
Can be used in SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, aggregations
CASE must end with END keyword

interactiveQA.question: CASE is similar to which programming concept?
interactiveQA.explanation: CASE works exactly like IF-ELSE logic in programming. You define conditions (WHEN), specify results (THEN), and provide a default (ELSE).

interactiveQA.question: Which type of CASE is most commonly used in real-world scenarios?
interactiveQA.explanation: Searched CASE allows flexible conditions (>, <, BETWEEN, LIKE, etc.) making it more powerful than Simple CASE which only checks equality.
interactiveQA.memoryTrick: Search = flexible 🧠 (Use conditions, not just equality)

interactiveQA.question: What happens if no WHEN condition matches and there's no ELSE clause?
interactiveQA.explanation: Without ELSE, unmatched rows return NULL. This can cause issues in calculations and reports. Always include ELSE for safety!
interactiveQA.memoryTrick: No ELSE = NULL ❌ (Always provide a default)

interactiveQA.question: What is CASE primarily used for?
interactiveQA.answer: Applying conditional logic and transforming data
interactiveQA.explanation: CASE transforms raw data into meaningful categories, applies business rules, and enables conditional calculations - all within SQL queries.

interactiveQA.question: Can CASE be used inside aggregate functions like SUM?
interactiveQA.explanation: CASE inside aggregations is powerful: SUM(CASE WHEN status='paid' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) calculates conditional totals.

interactiveQA.question: What is the main benefit of CASE statements in reporting?
interactiveQA.explanation: CASE converts raw data (numbers, codes) into human-readable categories (High/Medium/Low, Active/Inactive) making reports understandable.

codingChallenge.title: Categorize Customer Salary
codingChallenge.scenario: Your company wants to classify customers based on their salary levels for targeted marketing campaigns. Create salary categories: High (>100k), Medium (50k-100k), and Low (<50k).
codingChallenge.problem: Write a query to classify each employee's salary into High, Medium, or Low categories.
codingChallenge.expectedOutput:
name | salary | category
Ankit | 120000 | High
Ravi | 70000 | Medium
Neha | 40000 | Low
Priya | 95000 | Medium
Amit | 30000 | Low
hints: Step 1: Understand requirement → categorization based on salary ranges
Step 3: Use CASE with WHEN conditions
Step 4: Add ELSE for values below 50k
Step 5: Use BETWEEN or comparison operators
Step 6: Give the result column an alias (AS category)
codingChallenge.solution:
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  CASE 
    WHEN salary > 100000 THEN 'High'
    WHEN salary BETWEEN 50000 AND 100000 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Low'
  END AS category
FROM employees
ORDER BY salary DESC;
codingChallenge.explanation: We use Searched CASE to evaluate salary ranges. The conditions are checked top-to-bottom: first >100k (High), then 50k-100k (Medium), and ELSE catches everything below 50k (Low). BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends. The result is aliased as 'category' for clarity.

quiz.question: CASE statement is most similar to which concept?
quiz.explanation: CASE implements conditional logic just like IF-ELSE in programming. It evaluates conditions and returns different results based on which condition is true.

quiz.question: What is CASE primarily used for in SQL?
quiz.explanation: CASE is used to apply conditional logic, transform data, and categorize values based on conditions - similar to IF-ELSE statements.

quiz.question: Which type of CASE is most commonly used?
quiz.explanation: Searched CASE is most flexible because it allows complex conditions (>, <, BETWEEN, LIKE) rather than just equality checks.

quiz.question: What happens if no WHEN condition matches and ELSE is not provided?
quiz.explanation: Without ELSE, unmatched conditions return NULL. This is why it's best practice to always include ELSE to handle unexpected cases.

quiz.question: Can CASE be used inside aggregate functions like SUM?
quiz.explanation: CASE inside aggregations is powerful: SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN value ELSE 0 END) enables conditional calculations.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of CASE in reporting?
quiz.explanation: CASE transforms raw data into meaningful categories, making reports human-readable (e.g., converting salary numbers to High/Medium/Low).

quiz.question: What keyword starts a CASE statement?
quiz.explanation: CASE statement syntax: CASE WHEN condition THEN result ... ELSE default END. It always starts with CASE and ends with END.

quiz.question: What keyword ends a CASE statement?
quiz.explanation: Every CASE statement must end with the END keyword. Forgetting END will cause a syntax error.

quiz.question: Where is CASE commonly used in data engineering?
quiz.explanation: CASE is heavily used in ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines to transform and categorize data during the loading process.

interviewAnswer: CASE statements in SQL are used to implement conditional logic similar to IF-ELSE. They help transform and categorize data dynamically based on conditions and are widely used in reporting, data transformation, and aggregations. Using CASE with aggregations enables powerful conditional analysis in real-world scenarios.
